abrasion.guidance: ACI 201.2R (Guide to Durable Concrete), abrasion section: for wear surfaces the compressive strength should in no case be less than 4000 psi (28 MPa), with low w/cm, hard aggregate, proper finishing and curing.

abrasion.guidance: ACI 302.1R (Guide to Concrete Floor and Slab Construction) recommended 28-day strength by floor class: light foot traffic classes 1-3 about 3000 psi (21 MPa); industrial vehicular classes 4-5 about 4000 psi (28 MPa); class 6 heavy industrial hard-wheeled traffic about 4500 psi (31 MPa); class 7 bonded topping 5000-8000 psi (35-55 MPa).
abrasion.citation: ACI 302.1R-04/-15 floor classification and strength table (handbook knowledge; not seen in tool output tonight; exact values differ slightly between editions)

abrasion.guidance: Upper bound for a wear slider: abrasion loss follows a power function of compressive strength, and no significant gain in abrasion resistance is found above 60 MPa.
abrasion.citation: Omoding N. et al., 'Review of Concrete Resistance to Abrasion by Waterborne Solids', ACI Materials Journal, 2020
abrasion.quote: no significant improvements in abrasion resistance can be gained by using concretes with compressive strengths exceeding 60 MPa (8.70 ksi)

notes: HOW TO READ 'sourced': the ACI 318 code text itself is paywalled and was not opened. The four w/cm-strength pairs and their MPa values (0.40/5000 psi/35 MPa; 0.45/4500/31; 0.50/4000/28; 0.55/3500/24) were seen VERBATIM in a Consensus MCP result (ACI Concrete International 2015, SIP 2). The mapping of pair to class (F1, F2, F3, S1, S2, S3, W1, W2, C2) was seen only in the built-in web search tool's own summary of third-party pages (TCA, open-exam-prep, ACI FAQ 904), which is a paraphrase, not verbatim page text; fetching those pages failed because the hosts are outside this session's network allowlist (nrmca.org, concrete.org, assets.noviams.com, open-exam-prep.com, theconstructor.org). All mappings match the well-known ACI 318-19 table. The 2500 psi (17 MPa) floor for F0, S0, W0, C0, C1 and all condition descriptions and sulfate thresholds are 'typical' (from memory), as are both ACI 201.2R / 302.1R abrasion strengths. Other requirements in the same table that the app does not model: air content for F1-F3, cement type and SCM limits for S1-S3, chloride ion limits for C0-C2, and SCM caps for F3. A mix in several classes must meet the most restrictive (lowest w/cm, highest f'c). MPa values are ACI's soft metric conversions. Label on page suggestion: 'ACI 318-19 Table 19.3.2.1 values, via secondary sources'.
